description: Dynamite Lumpia is a Filipino appetizer made from long green chilies stuffed with cheese or meat, wrapped in spring roll wrappers, and fried until crisp.
ingredients: 100 g cheddar cheese, cut into strips
steps: Wearing gloves, slit each chili lengthwise and remove the seeds if desired.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic and onion, then add the ground pork.
Add soy sauce and pepper. Cook until the pork is fully done.
Allow the filling to cool.
Stuff each chili with a little pork mixture and a strip of cheese.
Wrap each chili in a lumpia wrapper and seal the edges with water.
Fry until golden brown and crisp.
Drain and serve.
tips: Use gloves when handling chilies.
Remove more seeds and membranes to reduce heat.
Allow the filling to cool before wrapping.

name: Crispy Calamares
description: Crispy Calamares consists of squid rings coated in seasoned flour and deep-fried until golden brown. It is a common Filipino restaurant appetizer.
steps: Cut the cleaned squid into rings.
Pat the squid dry with paper towels.
In one bowl, whisk the egg and milk.
In another bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Dip the squid rings into the egg mixture.
Coat them evenly with the flour mixture.
Heat oil in a deep pan.
Fry the squid in small batches until lightly golden.
Drain and serve immediately.
tips: Dry squid thoroughly to help the coating adhere.
Fry in small batches to maintain oil temperature.
Avoid prolonged cooking because squid can become tough.

name: Crispy Chicken Skin
description: Crispy Chicken Skin is a crunchy appetizer made from seasoned chicken skin fried until crisp. It is often served with vinegar or spicy dipping sauce.
steps: Wash and handle the chicken skin safely, then pat it very dry.
Cut the skin into manageable pieces.
Combine flour, cornstarch, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Toss the chicken skin in the seasoned flour mixture.
Heat oil in a deep pan.
Fry the chicken skin in batches until golden and crisp.
Drain on a wire rack.
Allow the pieces to cool briefly before serving.
tips: Dry the chicken skin thoroughly to minimize oil splatter.
Use a splatter screen if available.
Keep the oil at a stable temperature.

name: Crispy Isaw
description: Isaw is a Filipino street-food favorite made from cleaned chicken intestines that are boiled, seasoned, skewered, and grilled. This version is grilled for a smoky flavor.
steps: Clean the intestines thoroughly according to safe food-handling practices.
Place them in a pot with water, vinegar, garlic, ginger, salt, and pepper.
Simmer until tender and fully cooked.
Drain and cool enough to handle.
Thread the intestines onto bamboo skewers.
Combine soy sauce, calamansi juice, and oil.
Grill the skewers, brushing them with the mixture.
Turn frequently until lightly charred.
Serve hot with spiced vinegar.
tips: Purchase intestines from a reputable supplier and clean them carefully.
Boiling does not replace thorough cleaning.
Ensure the intestines are fully cooked before grilling.

name: Turon
description: Turon is a Filipino fried snack made from sliced saba bananas, often with jackfruit, wrapped in lumpia wrappers and coated with caramelized sugar.
steps: Place a banana half and a few strips of jackfruit on each wrapper.
Sprinkle a little brown sugar over the filling.
Fold the sides inward and roll tightly.
Seal the edge with water.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the rolls until golden brown.
Sprinkle additional brown sugar into the pan carefully and allow it to caramelize around the turon, if desired.
Drain and serve warm.
tips: Roll the wrappers tightly to prevent filling from leaking.
Watch the sugar carefully because it can burn quickly.
Use ripe but firm saba bananas.

name: Maruya
description: Maruya is a Filipino banana fritter made by coating sliced saba bananas in a simple batter and frying them until golden brown.
steps: Peel the bananas and slice them lengthwise or fan them out.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add the egg and milk or water.
Mix until a smooth batter forms.
Dip the bananas into the batter.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the coated bananas until golden brown on both sides.
Drain excess oil.
Sprinkle with sugar if desired and serve warm.
tips: Avoid overmixing the batter.
Maintain moderate heat to cook the batter without burning the outside.
PART 3: MEAT-BASED FILIPINO APPETIZERS

name: Pork Siomai
description: Pork siomai is a Filipino-style dumpling filled with ground pork, vegetables, and seasonings, wrapped in thin wonton wrappers and steamed.
steps: Combine the ground pork, carrots, onion, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, pepper, and water.
Mix until the filling is evenly combined.
Place approximately 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of each wrapper.
Gather the wrapper around the filling, leaving the top open.
Arrange the siomai in a lightly oiled steamer.
Steam over boiling water until the pork is fully cooked, approximately 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve hot with soy sauce, calamansi, and chili garlic sauce.
tips: Do not overfill the wrappers.
Leave space between the dumplings to allow steam to circulate.
Ensure the filling reaches 71°C.

name: Chicken Siomai
description: A Filipino-style adaptation of siomai, a steamed dumpling filled with ground chicken, carrots, onions, and seasonings.
steps: Combine the ground chicken, carrots, onion, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, pepper, and water.
Mix thoroughly.
Place a tablespoon of filling in each wrapper.
Shape into dumplings.
Arrange the dumplings in a lightly greased steamer.
Steam until the chicken filling reaches an internal temperature of 74°C.
Serve hot with soy sauce and calamansi.
tips: Keep raw chicken separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.
Wash hands and utensils after handling raw chicken.
Avoid stacking the dumplings too closely.

name: Pork Embutido Slices
description: Embutido is a Filipino steamed or baked meatloaf made with ground pork, vegetables, eggs, and seasonings. It is often sliced and served as an appetizer.
steps: Combine ground pork, eggs, carrots, breadcrumbs, raisins, pickle relish, cheese, onion, garlic, soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Mix until evenly combined.
Divide the mixture into portions.
Shape each portion into a log and wrap securely in food-grade foil.
Place the wrapped logs in a steamer.
Steam until the center reaches 71°C.
Allow the embutido to rest before unwrapping.
Slice into rounds and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Avoid packing the mixture too tightly.
Cool completely before slicing for cleaner cuts.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly.

name: Pork Barbecue Skewers
description: Filipino pork barbecue consists of marinated pork slices grilled on skewers. It is commonly served at parties, street-food stalls, and family gatherings.
steps: Combine soy sauce, banana ketchup, calamansi juice, sugar, garlic, pepper, and oil.
Add the pork and mix until coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Thread the pork onto soaked bamboo skewers.
Preheat a grill to medium heat.
Grill the skewers, turning frequently.
Brush with reserved marinade only if it has been handled safely and boiled before use.
Continue grilling until the pork reaches a safe internal temperature.
Serve hot.
tips: Slice the pork evenly for uniform cooking.
Do not reuse uncooked marinade as a dipping sauce.
Soak bamboo skewers in water before grilling.

name: Chicken Inasal Bites
description: Chicken inasal is a Filipino grilled chicken preparation associated with Bacolod. This appetizer version uses small boneless chicken pieces marinated in calamansi, vinegar, garlic, and annatto.
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Combine calamansi juice, vinegar, garlic, soy sauce, oil, annatto powder, salt, and pepper.
Add the chicken and mix well.
Refrigerate for 1 to 2 hours.
Thread the chicken pieces onto soaked bamboo skewers.
Grill over medium heat, turning frequently.
Continue cooking until the chicken reaches 74°C internally.
Serve with calamansi and soy sauce dipping mixture.
tips: Use separate utensils for raw and cooked chicken.
Avoid charring the outside before the inside is cooked.
Smaller pieces cook faster, so monitor them closely.

name: Chicken Pastel Bites
description: Chicken pastel is a Filipino adaptation of a savory chicken pie or casserole, commonly made with chicken, vegetables, and a creamy sauce. This version uses small pastry cups for appetizer portions.
steps: Melt butter in a pan and sauté garlic and onion.
Add the chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add carrots and potatoes.
Pour in chicken broth and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in flour and evaporated milk.
Add peas, salt, and pepper.
Simmer until the filling thickens and the chicken reaches 74°C.
Cool slightly and spoon into the pastry shells.
Serve warm.
tips: Dice the vegetables evenly.
Allow the filling to thicken before placing it in the pastry shells.
Fill the pastry cups shortly before serving to preserve crispness.

name: Beef Lumpia
description: Beef lumpia is a Filipino spring roll variation filled with ground beef, carrots, onions, and seasonings.
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add ground beef and cook until browned and fully cooked.
Add carrots, soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Cook until the carrots are slightly tender and the mixture is not watery.
Cool the filling.
Place a spoonful of filling on each wrapper.
Fold and roll tightly, sealing the edges with water.
Fry until golden brown.
Drain and serve.
tips: Drain excess fat from the beef filling before wrapping.
Allow the filling to cool before assembly.
Ensure the beef reaches an internal temperature of 71°C.

name: Pork Sisig Cups
description: Sisig is a Filipino dish commonly associated with Pampanga. It typically consists of chopped pork seasoned with calamansi, onion, chili, and other seasonings. This version is served in small appetizer cups.
ingredients: 300 g cooked pork belly or pork shoulder
½ tsp salt, or to taste
12 small lettuce leaves or crisp edible cups
steps: Cut the cooked pork into small pieces.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Add the pork and cook until lightly crisp.
Add the onion and chili.
Season with soy sauce, calamansi juice, salt, and pepper.
Toss until well combined.
Spoon the mixture into lettuce leaves or appetizer cups.
Serve immediately.
tips: Use fully cooked pork.
Prepare the onion and calamansi shortly before serving for freshness.
If using leftover pork, reheat it thoroughly.

name: Pork Dinakdakan
description: Dinakdakan is a traditional Ilocano dish made from grilled or boiled pork, onions, chili, and a creamy dressing. It is usually served as pulutan but can also be portioned as an appetizer.
ingredients: 400 g pork face or pork shoulder
½ tsp salt, or to taste
steps: Boil the pork until tender and fully cooked.
Grill the pork until lightly charred.
Cut the pork into small pieces.
In a bowl, combine calamansi juice, vinegar, soy sauce, mayonnaise, salt, and pepper.
Add the pork, onion, and chili.
Mix gently until coated.
Serve immediately or refrigerate briefly before serving.
tips: Cook pork thoroughly before grilling.
Add the mayonnaise after the pork has cooled slightly.
Keep the finished dish chilled if not serving immediately.

name: Beef Empanada Bites
description: Filipino empanadas are pastry pockets filled with savory meat, vegetables, and seasonings. This appetizer version uses smaller portions of beef filling.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion.
Add ground beef and cook until browned.
Add potatoes, carrots, peas, soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Cook until the vegetables are tender and the filling is relatively dry.
Cool the filling.
Combine flour and butter in a bowl until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add egg and enough cold water to form a dough.
Roll out the dough and cut into small circles.
Place filling in the center of each circle, fold, and crimp the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 180°C until golden brown and cooked through.
tips: Keep the pastry dough cold for a flakier texture.
Avoid adding too much filling.
Cool the filling before assembling the empanadas.
PART 4: SEAFOOD FILIPINO APPETIZERS

name: Shrimp Gambas
description: Shrimp gambas is a Filipino-style appetizer featuring shrimp sautéed with garlic, butter or oil, and chili. It is commonly served in restaurants and at gatherings.
steps: Clean the shrimp and pat dry.
Heat butter and oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the bell pepper and chili.
Add the shrimp and cook, stirring occasionally.
Season with calamansi juice, salt, and pepper.
Cook until the shrimp are opaque and fully cooked.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot.
tips: Avoid overcooking shrimp because they become rubbery.
Keep raw seafood separate from cooked food.
Add calamansi near the end to preserve its fresh flavor.

name: Garlic Butter Shrimp
description: Garlic butter shrimp is a simple Filipino restaurant-style appetizer made by sautéing shrimp in butter, garlic, and seasonings.
steps: Clean and dry the shrimp.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat.
Add garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and toss to coat.
Add water, calamansi juice, salt, and pepper.
Cook until the shrimp are opaque and fully cooked.
Sprinkle with parsley if desired.
Serve immediately.
tips: Use medium heat to prevent the garlic from burning.
Avoid adding excessive water, which can dilute the butter sauce.
Cook shrimp in a single layer when possible.

name: Tortang Dulong
description: Tortang Dulong is a Filipino fish omelet made from small silver fish mixed with eggs, onions, and seasonings, then pan-fried.
steps: Rinse the dulong carefully and drain well.
In a bowl, beat the eggs.
Add the fish, onion, garlic, flour, salt, and pepper.
Mix gently.
Heat oil in a nonstick pan.
Spoon small portions of the mixture into the pan.
Cook until the underside is golden and the mixture begins to set.
Flip carefully and cook the other side.
Ensure the fish and egg mixture is fully cooked.
Serve warm.
tips: Drain the fish thoroughly to prevent a watery mixture.
Make small fritters for easier flipping.
Cook over medium heat to prevent burning.

name: Tuna Croquettes
description: A Filipino home-style appetizer variation of breaded tuna patties, flavored with calamansi and made with common pantry ingredients.
ingredients: 1 can tuna in water, approximately 185 g, drained
½ cup breadcrumbs, plus extra for coating
steps: Drain the tuna thoroughly.
Combine tuna, mashed potatoes, onion, egg, breadcrumbs, calamansi juice, salt, and pepper.
Mix until the ingredients hold together.
Shape into small oval patties.
Coat each patty in additional breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a pan.
Fry the croquettes in batches until golden brown.
Drain and serve warm.
tips: Remove excess moisture from the tuna and potatoes.
Chill the shaped croquettes for 15 to 20 minutes if they are too soft to handle.
Avoid overcrowding the pan.

name: Crab Stick Fritters
description: A Filipino-inspired party appetizer variation made with shredded imitation crab, vegetables, eggs, and flour, shaped into small savory fritters.
steps: Shred the crab sticks into small pieces.
Combine crab sticks, eggs, flour, carrots, spring onions, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Mix until the ingredients are evenly combined.
Heat oil in a nonstick pan.
Spoon small portions of the mixture into the pan.
Flatten gently with a spatula.
Cook until golden brown on one side.
Flip and cook the other side until set.
Serve warm.
tips: Make the fritters small so they hold together more easily.
Avoid adding extra water because the crab sticks already contain moisture.
Check package instructions for handling imitation crab.

name: Rellenong Pusit
description: Rellenong Pusit is stuffed squid filled with a savory mixture of vegetables and seasonings. It can be sliced into bite-sized rounds and served as an appetizer.
ingredients: 4 medium squid, cleaned and bodies kept whole
steps: Clean the squid and reserve the tentacles.
Chop the tentacles finely.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion.
Add ground pork and chopped tentacles.
Cook until the pork is fully cooked.
Add carrots, soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Cool the mixture, then combine with the egg.
Stuff each squid body loosely with the filling.
Secure the opening with a toothpick.
Pan-sear the squid over medium heat until the squid is cooked through and the filling reaches 71°C.
Rest briefly, slice into rounds, and serve.
tips: Do not overstuff the squid because the filling expands slightly during cooking.
Avoid overcooking the squid.
Remove all toothpicks before serving individual slices.

name: Grilled Tuna Belly Bites
description: Grilled tuna belly is a Filipino seafood favorite often seasoned with soy sauce, calamansi, garlic, and pepper. Smaller pieces make it suitable for appetizer platters.
ingredients: 400 g tuna belly, cut into small pieces
¼ tsp salt, or to taste
steps: Combine calamansi juice, soy sauce, garlic, oil, pepper, and salt.
Add the tuna belly and coat evenly.
Refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes.
Preheat a grill or grill pan.
Grill the tuna pieces, turning carefully.
Cook until the fish reaches 63°C internally.
Transfer to a platter and serve with calamansi.
tips: Cut the tuna into evenly sized pieces.
Avoid excessive marination because the citrus can change the texture of the fish.
Use a lightly oiled grill to reduce sticking.

name: Adobong Pusit Bites
description: Adobong Pusit is a Filipino squid dish cooked with vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, and pepper. This version uses small squid pieces and is served in appetizer portions.
ingredients: 400 g cleaned squid, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Heat oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the squid and stir briefly.
Add vinegar, soy sauce, bay leaf, pepper, and water.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the squid is tender and thoroughly cooked.
Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Remove the bay leaf.
Serve in small bowls.
tips: Squid cooks quickly, so avoid prolonged cooking unless using a method intended to tenderize it.
Do not overcrowd the pan.
Keep the finished dish refrigerated if not serving immediately.

name: Tinolang Tahong
description: Tinolang Tahong is a Filipino mussel soup flavored with ginger, garlic, onion, and leafy vegetables. It can be served in small cups as a warm appetizer.
ingredients: ½ tsp salt, or to taste
steps: Scrub the mussels and remove the beards.
Discard mussels with broken shells or those that remain open when tapped.
Heat oil in a pot.
Sauté ginger, garlic, and onion.
Add the mussels and water.
Bring to a boil and cover.
Cook until the mussels open and are fully cooked.
Discard any mussels that remain closed after cooking.
Add the leafy vegetables and simmer briefly.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot in small cups.
tips: Buy mussels from a reputable supplier.
Keep live mussels cold before cooking.
Never consume mussels that remain closed after cooking.

name: Fried Tilapia Fingers
description: A Filipino-style seafood appetizer made from tilapia fillet strips coated in seasoned breading and fried until crisp; serve with calamansi or a dipping sauce.
steps: Cut the tilapia fillets into strips.
Pat the fish dry.
Combine flour, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish.
Dredge each fish strip in the flour mixture.
Dip into the beaten egg.
Coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the fish strips until golden brown and the fish reaches 63°C internally.
Drain on a wire rack.
Serve hot.
tips: Keep the coating light and even.
Avoid overcrowding the pan.
Use a thermometer to check doneness when possible.
PART 5: VEGETABLE-BASED AND FILIPINO-INSPIRED APPETIZERS

name: Tortang Talong
description: Tortang Talong is a Filipino eggplant omelet made by grilling or boiling eggplant, flattening it, dipping it in beaten egg, and pan-frying it.
steps: Grill or boil the eggplants until tender.
Allow them to cool enough to handle.
Peel away the skin while keeping the stems attached.
Flatten each eggplant gently with a fork.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Dip each eggplant into the egg mixture.
Heat oil in a pan.
Fry the eggplants until golden on both sides and the egg is fully cooked.
Serve warm.
tips: Grill the eggplants for a smoky flavor.
Flatten gently to avoid breaking the flesh.
Cook over medium heat to ensure the egg sets properly.

name: Okoy na Kalabasa
description: Okoy na Kalabasa is a Filipino fritter made from grated squash mixed with flour, egg, and seasonings. It is a vegetable-based variation of traditional okoy.
steps: Grate the squash and squeeze out excess liquid.
Combine the squash, flour, egg, garlic, onion, salt, and pepper.
Add a little water only if necessary to bind the mixture.
Heat oil in a pan.
Spoon small portions of the mixture into the hot oil.
Flatten each portion slightly.
Fry until golden brown.
Turn and cook the other side.
Drain and serve with vinegar.
tips: Remove excess moisture to help the fritters hold their shape.
Make small fritters for more even cooking.
Do not overcrowd the pan.

name: Camote Fries
description: A Filipino-inspired snack appetizer made from sweet potato strips, fried or baked until tender inside and crisp outside.
steps: Wash and peel the sweet potatoes.
Cut them into evenly sized strips.
Pat dry with a clean towel.
Toss with oil, salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
To bake, arrange in a single layer on a baking tray.
Bake at 220°C until tender and lightly crisp, turning halfway through.
Alternatively, fry in hot oil until golden and cooked through.
Serve immediately.
tips: Cut the strips evenly so they cook at the same rate.
Avoid overcrowding the baking tray.
Serve immediately for the best texture.

name: Ginisang Togue Cups
description: A Filipino-inspired appetizer variation of ginisang togue, with sautéed mung bean sprouts and vegetables served in small lettuce cups.
steps: Wash the bean sprouts and drain well.
Heat oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic and onion.
Add tofu and cook until lightly browned.
Add carrots and stir-fry briefly.
Add bean sprouts and soy sauce.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook until the vegetables are just tender.
Allow the mixture to cool slightly.
Spoon into clean lettuce leaves and serve.
tips: Cook bean sprouts thoroughly.
Drain the vegetables well to prevent excess liquid from collecting in the lettuce cups.
Assemble the cups shortly before serving.

name: Pritong Tokwa
description: A familiar Filipino-style tofu appetizer of golden fried tofu cubes served with a vinegar, soy sauce, onion, and chili dip.
steps: Drain the tofu and pat it dry thoroughly.
Cut into bite-sized cubes.
Heat oil in a deep pan.
Fry the tofu until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on a wire rack or paper towels.
Combine vinegar, soy sauce, onion, garlic, chili, and pepper in a small bowl.
Place the fried tofu on a serving plate.
Serve with the dipping sauce.
tips: Press tofu briefly before frying to remove excess moisture.
Dry tofu thoroughly to reduce oil splatter.
Serve soon after frying to maintain crispness.

name: Lumpiang Puso ng Saging
description: Lumpiang Puso ng Saging is a vegetable spring roll filled with cooked banana blossom and seasonings. It is a practical way to incorporate a traditional Filipino vegetable into an appetizer.
steps: Remove the tough outer layers of the banana blossom.
Chop the blossom and soak briefly in salted water.
Drain and rinse thoroughly.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic and onion.
Add banana blossom and carrots.
Season with soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Cook until tender and most excess moisture has evaporated.
Cool the filling.
Place a spoonful of filling on each wrapper and roll tightly.
Fry until golden brown.
Drain and serve.
tips: Remove tough parts of the banana blossom.
Drain the filling well before wrapping.
Allow the filling to cool to prevent the wrappers from becoming soggy.

name: Kwek-Kwek-Style Quail Egg Salad Bites
description: A Filipino-inspired no-fry appetizer that pairs boiled quail eggs with a tomato, onion, and vinegar dressing, served in lettuce cups.
ingredients: ½ small red onion, finely chopped
steps: Hard-boil the quail eggs and cool them.
Peel the eggs and cut each in half.
Combine tomatoes, onion, vinegar, calamansi juice, salt, and pepper.
Add chili if desired.
Place small portions of the tomato mixture on lettuce leaves.
Top each with two quail egg halves.
Arrange on a serving platter.
Serve immediately.
tips: Use clean utensils and chilled ingredients.
Prepare the tomato mixture shortly before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly.

name: Fresh Lumpiang Ubod
description: Fresh Lumpiang Ubod is a Filipino spring roll made with heart of palm, vegetables, and a soft wrapper. It is commonly served with a sweet-savory garlic sauce.
ingredients: 2 cups ubod, cut into thin strips
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Heat oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic and onion.
Add ubod, carrots, and cabbage.
Add water, salt, and pepper.
Cook until the vegetables are tender and the liquid has mostly evaporated.
Whisk the flour, egg, water, and oil to prepare the wrapper batter.
Cook thin wrappers in a lightly greased nonstick pan.
Combine the sauce ingredients in a saucepan, then thicken with the cornstarch slurry.
Place filling on each wrapper and fold the sides inward.
Drizzle with sauce and serve.
tips: Slice ubod evenly for consistent texture.
Drain the filling well.
Keep the sauce separate until serving to prevent soggy wrappers.

name: Puto Pao
description: Puto Pao is a Filipino steamed rice cake with a savory filling, often made with pork asado. It combines the soft texture of puto with a flavorful meat center.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic and onion.
Add pork and cook until browned.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and water.
Simmer until the pork is tender and the sauce has thickened. Ensure the pork is fully cooked.
Allow the filling to cool.
Combine flour, sugar, and baking powder in a bowl.
Add egg, milk, and melted butter. Mix until smooth.
Fill small greased molds halfway with batter.
Add a small amount of pork filling.
Cover with more batter.
Steam until the cakes are set and a toothpick inserted into the batter comes out clean.
Cool slightly before removing from the molds.
tips: Do not overfill the molds.
Avoid lifting the steamer lid too often because it can interrupt cooking.
Keep the filling relatively dry to prevent the cakes from becoming soggy.

name: Bibingkang Malagkit Bites
description: Bibingkang Malagkit is a Filipino sticky rice cake made with glutinous rice, coconut milk, and sugar, often topped with a caramelized coconut mixture. Small squares can be served as a sweet appetizer or dessert bite.
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice until the water runs relatively clear.
Combine the rice and water in a pot.
Cook until the rice is partially tender and most of the water has been absorbed.
Add coconut milk, brown sugar, and salt.
Stir over low heat until the rice is fully cooked and the mixture becomes thick and sticky.
Transfer the mixture to a greased baking dish.
In a saucepan, combine coconut cream and brown sugar.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until the topping thickens.
Spread the topping over the rice mixture.
Bake at 180°C until the topping becomes darker and slightly caramelized.
Cool before cutting into small squares.
tips: Stir frequently to prevent the rice from sticking to the bottom of the pot.
Use low heat when cooking the coconut topping to avoid burning.
Allow the bibingka malagkit to cool before slicing.

name: Sinigang Na Baboy
description: A Filipino sour soup of tender pork simmered in tamarind broth with gabi and vegetables.
ingredients: 1 packet sinigang mix or ½ cup strained tamarind juice
Fish sauce and green chilies to taste
steps: Bring the water to a boil with the onion and tomatoes. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the pork and simmer until tender, skimming the surface as needed.
Stir in the tamarind or sinigang mix and taste the broth.
Add the firm vegetables and cook until they begin to soften.
Season with fish sauce and add chilies if desired.
Add the leafy vegetables and cook just until wilted.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Simmer the pork gently and add leafy vegetables last to preserve their color.

name: Sinigang Na Hipon
description: A quick shrimp sinigang with tamarind broth, tomatoes, radish, and kangkong.
ingredients: Fish sauce and green chilies to taste
steps: Bring the water, onion, and tomatoes to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind mix and add the radish or other firm vegetables.
Simmer until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Season the broth with fish sauce and adjust the sourness.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3–4 minutes, just until pink and opaque.
Add the leafy vegetables and turn off the heat when wilted.
Serve immediately with rice.
tips: Add shrimp near the end and cook only until pink and opaque.

name: Sinigang Na Bangus
description: Milkfish simmered in a tangy tamarind broth with gabi and classic sinigang vegetables.
ingredients: 1 medium bangus, cleaned and cut into steaks
steps: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes, and ginger to a gentle boil.
Simmer for 5 minutes to flavor the broth.
Add the firm vegetables and cook until nearly tender.
Lower the fish carefully into the broth and simmer gently until cooked.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add leafy greens and cook just until wilted.
Serve hot, taking care not to break the fish.
tips: Use a wide pot and avoid stirring after adding the fish so the pieces stay intact.

name: Sinigang Na Baka
description: A hearty beef soup with tamarind, tender beef, radish, and leafy vegetables.
ingredients: 750 g beef brisket or short ribs
steps: Place the beef and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Add onion and tomatoes, then simmer gently until the beef is tender.
Stir in the tamarind or sinigang mix.
Add gabi and other firm vegetables and cook until nearly tender.
Add the remaining vegetables and season with fish sauce.
Finish with leafy greens and cook until wilted.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Cook the beef until tender before adding the souring agent and vegetables.

name: Sinigang Na Salmon Belly
description: Salmon belly gives this tamarind soup a rich flavor while vegetables keep it bright and refreshing.
ingredients: 500 g salmon belly, cut into portions
steps: Bring water, onion, and tomatoes to a boil and simmer briefly.
Add tamarind mix and the firm vegetables; cook until nearly tender.
Season the broth with fish sauce.
Lower salmon pieces into the broth and simmer gently until just cooked.
Add leafy greens and turn off the heat when wilted.
Taste and adjust the sourness.
Serve hot immediately.
tips: Do not boil salmon for too long; it cooks quickly and can break apart.

name: Sinigang Na Isda Sa Miso
description: A sour fish soup enriched with sautéed miso, tomatoes, and tamarind for a deeper savory flavor.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion and tomatoes until softened.
Stir in miso and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in water and add the souring agent; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add radish and cook until nearly tender.
Lower fish into the broth and simmer gently until cooked.
Season with fish sauce and add leafy greens.
Serve hot.
tips: Dissolve the miso thoroughly and simmer gently after adding fish.

name: Sinigang Na Hipon Sa Bayabas
description: A Kapampangan-style sour soup that uses guava for a fragrant, mellow broth with shrimp and vegetables.
steps: Bring water, onion, and tomatoes to a boil. Add guavas and simmer until soft and fragrant.
Press some guava flesh into the broth; strain seeds if preferred.
Add the firm vegetables and cook until nearly tender.
Season with fish sauce and taste the broth.
Add the shrimp or fish and cook just until done.
Finish with leafy greens and serve hot.
tips: Use fragrant ripe guavas and strain the broth if you prefer fewer seeds.

name: Sinigang Na Isda Sa Kamias
description: A coastal-style fish soup soured with fresh kamias and finished with leafy greens.
steps: Bring water, kamias, onion, and tomatoes to a boil. Simmer to release the sour flavor.
Add the firm vegetables and cook until nearly tender.
Lower fish into the broth and simmer gently until cooked.
Season with fish sauce and adjust sourness.
Add leafy greens and cook just until wilted.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Taste the broth before adding more kamias because the fruits vary in sourness.

name: Sinigang Na Hipon Sa Sampalok At Gabi
description: Shrimp and gabi make a hearty version of the familiar tamarind soup, with a naturally fuller broth.
steps: Bring the water, onion, and tomatoes to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind mix and add the radish or other firm vegetables.
Simmer until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Season the broth with fish sauce and adjust the sourness.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3–4 minutes, just until pink and opaque.
Add the leafy vegetables and turn off the heat when wilted.
Serve immediately with rice.
tips: Cook gabi until soft and add shrimp only near serving time.

name: Sinigang Na Bangus Sa Bayabas
description: Milkfish and ripe guava create a mellow, fruity sour soup with radish and leafy vegetables.
ingredients: 1 medium bangus, cleaned and cut into steaks
steps: Bring water, onion, and tomatoes to a boil. Add guava and simmer until fragrant.
Mash some guava flesh into the broth and strain seeds if desired.
Add firm vegetables and simmer until nearly tender.
Season with fish sauce.
Lower bangus into the broth and simmer gently until cooked.
Add kangkong and serve hot.
tips: Remove guava seeds if desired and avoid stirring the fish.

name: Sinigang Na Hipon Sa Batwan
description: A Visayan-inspired shrimp soup using batwan, a traditional souring fruit in parts of the Visayas.
ingredients: 5–6 batwan fruits or 2 tbsp batwan paste
steps: Bring water, onion, and tomatoes to a boil. Add batwan and simmer until the broth turns pleasantly sour.
Add firm vegetables and cook until nearly tender.
Season with fish sauce and taste the broth.
Add seafood or meat according to the recipe and cook until done.
Finish with leafy greens if included.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Add batwan gradually; its sourness and intensity vary.

name: Sinigang Na Tilapia
description: A practical family fish sinigang made with tilapia, tamarind broth, and common vegetables.
ingredients: 2 medium tilapia, cleaned and cut into portions
steps: Bring the water, onion, tomatoes, and ginger to a gentle boil.
Simmer for 5 minutes to flavor the broth.
Add the firm vegetables and cook until nearly tender.
Lower the fish carefully into the broth and simmer gently until cooked.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add leafy greens and cook just until wilted.
Serve hot, taking care not to break the fish.
tips: Use fresh fish and avoid stirring once the tilapia is in the pot.

name: Bulalo
description: A Batangas favorite of beef shank and marrow bones slowly simmered until tender, with corn and pechay.
ingredients: 1.2 kg beef shank with marrow bone
Fish sauce and salt to taste
steps: Blanch the beef in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse the meat and pot.
Return beef to the pot with fresh water, onion, and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently until the meat is tender. Skim as needed.
Add corn and cook for 10 minutes.
Add potatoes and simmer until tender.
Season with fish sauce, then add cabbage and pechay.
Serve hot with a fish-sauce, calamansi, and chili dip.
tips: Blanch the beef first and maintain a gentle simmer for a clearer broth.

name: Nilagang Baka
description: A simple boiled beef soup with potatoes, corn, cabbage, and pechay in a clean savory broth.
ingredients: 1 kg beef brisket or short ribs
steps: Place the meat and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Add onion and peppercorns. Lower the heat and simmer until the meat is tender.
Add corn and cook for 8–10 minutes.
Add potatoes or other firm vegetables and cook until tender.
Season with fish sauce and salt.
Add cabbage and pechay; simmer briefly until just tender.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Skim the broth and add vegetables according to their cooking time.

name: Nilagang Baboy
description: A comforting pork nilaga with tender ribs, corn, potatoes, cabbage, and pechay.
steps: Place pork and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Add onion and peppercorns. Simmer until the pork is tender.
Add corn and cook for 8 minutes.
Add potatoes and simmer until fork-tender.
Season with fish sauce and salt.
Add cabbage and pechay and cook briefly.
Serve hot.
tips: Ribs make a richer broth; skim regularly for a cleaner soup.

name: Nilagang Pata
description: Pork hock simmered until the skin and meat are tender, served in a savory broth with vegetables.
steps: Blanch the pata in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Return pata to a pot with fresh water, onion, and peppercorns.
Simmer gently until the skin and meat are tender, adding water as needed.
Add corn and potatoes and cook until tender.
Season with fish sauce.
Add cabbage and pechay and simmer briefly.
Serve hot.
tips: Blanch and rinse the pata first to help produce a cleaner broth.

name: Cebuano Pochero (Pocherong Bisaya)
description: A Visayan clear-broth beef soup with corn, saba bananas, cabbage, and pechay.
steps: Place beef and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Add onion and peppercorns and simmer until the beef is tender.
Add corn and cook for 10 minutes.
Add saba and simmer until tender but still holding its shape.
Season with fish sauce and salt.
Add cabbage and pechay and cook until just tender.
Serve hot with the broth.
tips: Use firm saba and add it near the end so it keeps its shape.

name: Beef Lauya
description: A Northern Luzon-style beef soup slowly simmered with ginger, garlic, and peppercorns.
steps: Place beef and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Add onion, ginger, garlic, and peppercorns.
Simmer gently until beef is tender, adding hot water if needed.
Add optional saba and cook until tender.
Season lightly with fish sauce and salt.
Add cabbage and pechay and simmer briefly.
Serve hot.
tips: Keep seasoning simple to highlight the beef and ginger broth.

name: Linagpang Na Manok (Ilonggo Grilled Chicken Soup)
description: A Western Visayan soup made by grilling chicken first, then simmering it in a spicy broth of tomatoes, onion, ginger, spring onion, and guinamos.
ingredients: 2 stalks spring onion, cut into pieces
1 tbsp guinamos or fish sauce, to taste
steps: Season the chicken lightly with salt and pepper, then grill until cooked and lightly charred. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Pour in water or chicken stock and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the grilled chicken and simmer for 10–15 minutes so the flavors combine.
Season with guinamos or fish sauce. Add chilies and spring onion.
Simmer briefly, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.
tips: Grill the chicken until lightly charred for a smoky flavor, but avoid drying it out.

name: Kansi
description: A Negros beef-shank soup with unripe jackfruit and the distinctive sourness of batwan.
ingredients: Fish sauce and chilies to taste
steps: Place beef shank and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Add onion, tomatoes, ginger, and lemongrass. Simmer until the beef is tender.
Add batwan and simmer until the broth becomes pleasantly sour.
Add young jackfruit and cook until tender.
Season with fish sauce and add chilies if desired.
Taste and adjust the sourness.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Use batwan for the characteristic Ilonggo flavor; add the souring agent gradually.

name: Kadyos, Baboy Kag Langka (Kbl)
description: An Ilonggo soup of pork, pigeon peas, and young jackfruit, traditionally soured with batwan.
steps: If using dried kadyos, soak overnight and drain. Simmer in fresh water until partly tender.
Add pork and onion. Simmer gently until the pork and beans are tender.
Add young jackfruit and cook until soft.
Add batwan and simmer until the broth is pleasantly sour.
Season with fish sauce and add chilies if desired.
Add talbos ng kamote and cook until wilted.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Soak dried kadyos overnight for more even cooking.

name: Tiyula Itum
description: A Tausug black beef soup colored by toasted coconut and flavored with turmeric, ginger, and lemongrass.
ingredients: 1 cup grated coconut, toasted dark brown
1 thumb-size turmeric or 1 tsp ground turmeric
Fish sauce and chilies to taste
steps: Toast grated coconut in a dry pan, stirring, until deep brown. Cool and grind finely.
Pound or blend onion, garlic, ginger, and turmeric into a coarse paste.
Place beef and water in a pot; bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Add spice paste, lemongrass, and peppercorns. Simmer until beef is tender.
Stir in toasted coconut gradually until the broth turns dark.
Season with fish sauce and chilies.
Simmer briefly and serve hot.
tips: Toast coconut slowly until deep brown but not ashy or bitter.

name: Chicken Binakol
description: A Western Visayan chicken soup traditionally made with coconut water, young coconut meat, ginger, and lemongrass.
steps: Heat a little oil and sauté ginger and onion until fragrant. Add chicken and lightly brown.
Pour in coconut water and stock. Add lemongrass and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer until chicken is cooked through.
Add sayote and young coconut meat; cook until sayote is tender.
Season with fish sauce.
Add malunggay and turn off the heat when wilted.
Serve hot.
tips: Use unsweetened coconut water; add young coconut meat near the end.

name: Chicken Halang-Halang
description: A spicy Visayan chicken soup with coconut milk, ginger, lemongrass, and chilies.
steps: Sauté ginger, onion, and garlic in oil until fragrant. Add chicken and lightly brown.
Add lemongrass and stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer until chicken is cooked.
Add papaya or sayote and cook until nearly tender.
Pour in coconut milk and add chilies. Heat gently.
Season with fish sauce.
Add leafy greens and cook until wilted.
Serve hot.
tips: Add chilies gradually and keep the coconut milk at a gentle simmer.

name: Papaitan
description: A traditional Ilocano soup of thoroughly cleaned beef or goat innards with a carefully balanced bitter broth.
ingredients: 700 g cleaned beef or goat tripe and innards
Fish sauce and pepper to taste
steps: Blanch cleaned innards in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Simmer innards in fresh water until tender, skimming as needed.
Sauté garlic, onion, ginger, and tomatoes until softened.
Add sautéed aromatics to the pot and season with fish sauce and pepper.
Stir in a small amount of food-safe bile, taste, and add gradually.
Add chilies and simmer briefly.
Serve hot.
tips: Use only food-safe, properly handled bile and add it little by little to control bitterness.

name: Pinikpikan-Inspired Chicken Soup
description: A home-style Cordilleran-inspired chicken soup flavored with ginger and aromatics; this version uses ordinary chicken.
steps: Place chicken and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Add ginger, onion, garlic, and peppercorns.
Lower the heat and simmer until the chicken is cooked through.
Add sayote and cook until tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add leafy greens and cook until wilted.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: This is a home-style adaptation, not a reproduction of traditional ceremonial preparation.

name: Pork And Young Jackfruit Soup (Linat-Ang Baboy)
description: A Visayan-style pork soup with young jackfruit in a savory ginger broth.
steps: Place pork and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Add onion, ginger, garlic, and peppercorns. Simmer until pork is tender.
Add young jackfruit and cook until soft.
Season with fish sauce and adjust the broth.
Add pechay or malunggay and cook until wilted.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Use young unripe jackfruit, not sweet ripe jackfruit.

name: Pork And Tomato Soup (Kinamatisang Baboy)
description: A home-style pork soup in which ripe tomatoes form a light, savory broth with ginger and leafy vegetables.
ingredients: Fish sauce and pepper to taste
steps: Place pork and water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Add onion, ginger, and garlic. Simmer until pork is tender.
Add tomatoes and simmer until softened and blended into the broth.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add pechay and cook just until wilted.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Use ripe tomatoes and press some softened pieces into the broth for fuller flavor.

name: La Paz Batchoy
description: An Iloilo noodle soup with pork broth, miki, pork slices, liver, and toppings such as chicharon and toasted garlic.
steps: Simmer pork in stock with onion, garlic, and peppercorns until tender. Remove and slice the pork.
Strain and season the broth with fish sauce. Keep it hot.
Blanch liver slices briefly in simmering broth until just cooked.
Blanch miki noodles and divide among serving bowls.
Top noodles with sliced pork and liver.
Pour hot broth over each serving.
Finish with chicharon, fried garlic, and green onions.
tips: Cook liver briefly and add chicharon just before serving so it stays crisp.

name: Pancit Molo
description: An Ilonggo dumpling soup with pork-and-shrimp wontons in clear chicken broth, often topped with shredded chicken.
steps: Combine ground pork, chopped shrimp, onion, garlic, egg white, soy sauce, and pepper.
Place a teaspoon of filling in each wrapper. Moisten edges, fold, and seal firmly.
Bring chicken stock to a gentle boil and season to taste.
Add dumplings in batches and simmer until cooked through and floating.
Add shredded chicken if using and simmer briefly.
Adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with green onions and fried garlic.
tips: Seal wrappers firmly and cook dumplings in batches to avoid overcrowding.

name: Pancit Lomi
description: A Batangas-style thick noodle soup made with fresh miki, pork, liver, vegetables, and egg ribbons.
ingredients: Soy sauce and fish sauce to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork and cook until lightly browned; add liver and cook briefly.
Pour in stock and season with soy sauce and fish sauce. Bring to a boil.
Add vegetables and noodles; cook until noodles are tender.
Stir in cornstarch slurry gradually until lightly thickened.
Pour in beaten egg in a thin stream while stirring gently.
Serve hot.
tips: Add slurry gradually; lomi should be thick but still soupy.

name: Beef Mami
description: A Filipino noodle soup with tender beef, fresh miki noodles, and pechay in a deeply savory broth.
ingredients: Fried garlic, green onions, and calamansi
steps: Simmer beef in water with onion, ginger, and peppercorns until tender.
Remove beef, slice thinly, and strain the broth if desired.
Season broth with fish sauce and keep hot.
Blanch noodles and leafy greens separately.
Divide noodles, meat, and vegetables among bowls.
Pour hot broth over each serving.
Garnish with fried garlic and green onions; serve with calamansi.
tips: Blanch noodles separately to keep the broth clear.

name: Chicken Mami
description: A comforting chicken noodle soup with clear broth, shredded chicken, miki noodles, and leafy greens.
steps: Simmer chicken in stock with onion, ginger, and peppercorns until cooked.
Remove chicken, shred the meat, and strain the broth if desired.
Season broth with fish sauce and keep hot.
Blanch noodles and pechay separately.
Divide noodles and shredded chicken among bowls.
Pour hot broth over each serving and add pechay.
Garnish with fried garlic and green onions.
tips: Bone-in chicken creates a more flavorful broth; blanch noodles separately.

name: Chicken Sotanghon Soup
description: A Filipino glass-noodle soup with chicken, mushrooms, carrots, and annatto-colored broth.
steps: Poach chicken in stock until cooked. Remove, cool, and shred; reserve the broth.
Sauté garlic and onion in annatto oil until fragrant.
Add carrot and mushrooms, if included, and cook briefly.
Pour in reserved stock and season with fish sauce.
Add soaked sotanghon and simmer until tender.
Return chicken and stir in leafy vegetables.
Garnish and serve hot.
tips: Add sotanghon near serving time because it absorbs broth quickly.

name: Chicken Sopas
description: Creamy Filipino macaroni soup with chicken, vegetables, evaporated milk, and optional hotdogs.
steps: Poach chicken in stock until cooked. Remove, cool, and shred; reserve the broth.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil until fragrant.
Add carrots, corn, or optional hotdogs and cook briefly.
Pour in reserved stock and bring to a boil.
Add macaroni and cook until just tender.
Return chicken and add cabbage; stir in milk and heat gently.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve.
tips: Add milk at the end and avoid a hard boil; keep extra stock for reheating.

name: Laswa (Ilonggo Vegetable Soup)
description: An Iloilo-style mixed vegetable soup simmered in a light broth with shrimp and seasoned with guinamos or fish sauce.
ingredients: 3 cups water or light shrimp stock
½ cup saluyot or malunggay leaves
1 tbsp guinamos or fish sauce, to taste
steps: Bring the water or shrimp stock to a gentle boil with the onion.
Add kalabasa and simmer until it begins to soften.
Add shrimp, sitaw, eggplant, and okra. Simmer briefly.
Add patola and cook until the vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Season gradually with guinamos or fish sauce.
Stir in saluyot or malunggay and cook just until wilted.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Add vegetables according to their cooking time and avoid overcooking the leafy greens.

name: Sinuwam Na Tahong (Bicol Mussel Soup)
description: A Bicol regional mussel soup cooked in a fragrant broth of ginger, garlic, onion, chilies, and chili leaves.
ingredients: 1 kg fresh mussels, scrubbed and debearded
1 bunch dahon ng sili or malunggay leaves
Fish sauce and ground pepper to taste
steps: Rinse and clean the mussels. Discard cracked mussels and those that remain open when tapped.
Heat oil in a pot. Sauté garlic, ginger, onion, and chilies until fragrant.
Add the mussels and stir for about 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook until the mussel shells open.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Discard mussels that remain closed after cooking.
Stir in chili leaves, allow them to wilt, and serve immediately.
tips: Do not overcook the mussels; discard any that remain closed after cooking.

name: Linarang Na Isda (Cebuano Sour Fish Soup)
description: A Cebuano fish soup with a sour-spicy tomato broth flavored with ginger, tausi, and kamias.
ingredients: 1 kg firm fish steaks or cleaned small whole fish
2 tbsp tausi, rinsed and lightly crushed
Fish sauce and black pepper to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Stir in tausi, then pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Add kamias and chilies. Simmer for 5 minutes to flavor the broth.
Lower the fish into the broth and simmer gently until fully cooked.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. Taste and adjust the sourness.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Use firm fish and avoid vigorous stirring so the pieces remain intact.

name: Sinanglaw (Ilocano Beef Innards Soup)
description: A traditional Ilocano beef soup made with tender beef and innards in a ginger-rich broth with sour and slightly bitter notes.
ingredients: 500 g cleaned beef tripe, pre-boiled until tender
500 g beef brisket, cut into bite-size pieces
1–2 tbsp food-safe beef bile, added gradually
Salt and ground pepper to taste
steps: If needed, pre-boil the tripe until tender. Drain and cut into bite-size pieces.
Heat a little oil in a pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the brisket, tripe, and optional innards. Stir briefly and season with fish sauce.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, and skim the surface.
Lower the heat and simmer until all the meat is tender.
Add kamias and simmer for 10–15 minutes. Stir in a small amount of food-safe bile gradually, tasting as you go.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, then serve hot with rice.
tips: Clean the innards thoroughly and add bile little by little; too much can make the broth unpleasantly bitter.

name: Suam Na Mais
description: A Kapampangan corn soup traditionally made with grated white corn, shrimp, and leafy greens.
ingredients: 4 ears fresh white corn, grated or scraped
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Pour in water or shrimp stock and bring to a simmer.
Stir in grated corn and cook until the broth thickens, stirring often.
Add shrimp and simmer until pink and opaque.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add leafy greens and cook until wilted.
Serve hot.
tips: Stir often after adding corn so it does not stick to the pot.

name: Dinengdeng
description: An Ilocano vegetable soup seasoned with bagoong isda and commonly served with grilled fish.
steps: Bring water to a boil with onion and tomatoes.
Stir in bagoong isda and simmer briefly; strain if preferred.
Add kalabasa and cook until partly tender.
Add sitaw and okra and simmer until just tender.
Add ampalaya and cook briefly.
Stir in saluyot or alugbati until wilted.
Top with grilled fish and serve hot.
tips: Add bagoong gradually because saltiness varies; use seasonal vegetables.

name: Utan Bisaya
description: A Visayan everyday vegetable soup made with seasonal vegetables in a light broth; fish may be added for extra flavor.
ingredients: 6 cups water or light fish stock
steps: Bring water or stock to a boil with onion and tomatoes.
Add kalabasa and sayote and simmer until partly tender.
Add sitaw and okra and cook until just tender.
Stir in cooked flaked fish if using.
Season with fish sauce.
Add leafy greens and cook until wilted.
Serve hot with rice.
tips: Use seasonal vegetables and add delicate leaves at the end.

name: Bulanglang Kapampangan
description: A simple Kapampangan vegetable soup with tomatoes and seasonal vegetables, often served alongside grilled or fried fish.
ingredients: Fish sauce or bagoong to taste
steps: Bring water, tomatoes, and onion to a boil. Simmer until the tomatoes soften.
Add kalabasa and cook until partly tender.
Add sitaw, eggplant, and okra. Simmer until just tender.
Season lightly with fish sauce or bagoong.
Add leafy greens and cook until wilted.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot, often alongside grilled fish and rice.
tips: Keep the seasoning light so the vegetables remain the focus.

name: Bulanglang Na Hipon
description: A Kapampangan sour soup pairing shrimp and guava with vegetables and water spinach.
steps: Bring water, onion, and tomatoes to a boil.
Add guavas and simmer until soft and fragrant.
Press some guava flesh into the broth; strain seeds if preferred.
Add sitaw and eggplant and cook until nearly tender.
Season with fish sauce.
Add shrimp and cook until pink; finish with kangkong.
Serve hot.
tips: Use fragrant guavas and taste before adding extra souring ingredients.

name: Sinabawang Tahong
description: Fresh mussels cooked in a clear ginger broth with tomatoes and leafy greens.
ingredients: 1 kg fresh mussels, scrubbed and debearded
steps: Discard mussels with cracked shells or those that remain open when tapped.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté ginger and onion until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Add mussels, cover, and cook until shells open.
Season with fish sauce and pepper; discard mussels that remain closed.
Add leafy greens, allow them to wilt, and serve immediately.
tips: Discard mussels that remain closed after cooking; do not overcook those that open.

name: Kusidong Isda
description: A Bicolano-style clear fish soup with tomatoes, ginger, leafy greens, and a calamansi finish.
steps: Bring water, ginger, onion, and tomatoes to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add fish pieces and cook gently until just cooked.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add leafy greens and cook until wilted.
Turn off the heat and stir in calamansi juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately with rice.
tips: Add calamansi off the heat for a fresher citrus aroma.

name: Linagpang Na Bangus
description: An Iloilo-style soup featuring grilled milkfish briefly simmered in a tomato-onion broth.
ingredients: 6 cups water or light fish stock
steps: Season and grill the bangus until cooked and lightly charred.
In a pot, bring water or fish stock, tomatoes, onion, and ginger to a boil.
Simmer until the vegetables soften and flavor the broth.
Add fish sauce and chilies.
Break grilled bangus into large portions and add to the broth.
Simmer briefly, add greens, and finish with calamansi.
Serve hot.
tips: Grill until lightly charred but not dry; remove large bones before serving.

name: Pesang Isda
description: A mild Filipino fish soup with ginger, onion, peppercorns, and leafy vegetables.
ingredients: 500 g fish, cut into serving pieces
steps: Combine water, ginger, onion, and peppercorns in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 5 minutes to flavor the broth.
Add sayote and cook until nearly tender.
Add fish carefully and simmer gently until cooked.
Season with fish sauce and salt.
Add pechay and cook until just wilted.
Serve hot.
tips: Keep the broth at a gentle simmer so the fish does not break apart.

name: Sinabawang Isda At Gulay
description: A simple Filipino fish-and-vegetable soup with tomatoes, ginger, and seasonal greens.
steps: Bring water, ginger, onion, and tomatoes to a boil.
Simmer briefly to flavor the broth.
Add sayote and cook until nearly tender.
Lower fish into the broth and simmer gently until cooked.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add pechay and cook until wilted.
Serve immediately.
tips: Choose firm fresh fish and avoid vigorous stirring.

name: Chicken Soup With Patola And Misua
description: A familiar Filipino soup combining chicken, patola, and thin misua noodles in a light broth.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in stock and simmer until chicken is cooked through.
Add patola and cook until tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Add misua and stir gently until softened.
Serve immediately while hot.
tips: Misua softens quickly; add it only when the patola is nearly tender.
